label: From an alignment to pair features: the outer-product mean
context: Left: an MSA drawn as a grid of 8 sequences (rows) × 10 residue columns, letters coloured by amino-acid class (use letters like A, L, K, E, G…). Highlight two columns i and j (blue and warm). Animate: for each sequence row, the features of column i and column j form a small outer-product square (draw a 3×3 tile from the two vectors); the 8 tiles stack and average into one tile labelled 'mean over sequences'; this tile is linearly projected and added into cell (i, j) of a 10×10 pair matrix z on the right, which brightens. Then sweep to other column pairs; cells fill in. Caption: 'columns that mutate together (co-evolution) produce a strong signal in z_ij'. Show two columns that co-vary (when one letter changes in a row, the other changes too) to make the point. Final caption: 'the MSA module turns co-evolution into pair features; AF3 runs 4 such blocks before the Pairformer'. Canvas is responsive: width anywhere from 340 to 900 px, height 400 px; derive every size and position from width and height, keep all text at least 11 px and fully inside the canvas, and on narrow widths stack or shrink rather than overlap. Loop forever on a cycle of 10 to 16 s with smooth easing between phases. White background. Put a one-line phase caption at the top centre that changes with the phase. No title inside the canvas (the card has one). Use plain sans-serif labels.

spec.title: From an alignment to pair features: the outer-product mean
spec.caption: For each pair of MSA columns (i, j), the per-sequence outer products xᵢ ⊗ xⱼ are averaged over sequences, linearly projected and added into zᵢⱼ. Columns that co-vary give a strong entry.
